objective.statement: Use a tie to join two notes of the same pitch into one longer sound.
successCriteria: I know a tie adds the two lengths together.
I can find one note that lasts as long as two tied notes.

explanation.text: A tie is a curved line joining two notes of the same pitch. You play the first note, and keep it going for the length of the second. You do not play the second note again.

music.textAlternative: A minim tied to a crotchet, shown with a curved line between them.

explanation.caption: A minim tied to a crotchet lasts 2 + 1 = 3 beats.

explanation.text: Add the two lengths together. A crotchet tied to a crotchet is 2 beats, the same as a minim. A minim tied to a minim is 4 beats, the same as a semibreve.
A tie lets a note last longer than any single note value can, or carry over a bar-line. You will see this in the next unit.

music.textAlternative: A crotchet tied to a crotchet, then a minim tied to a minim.

steps: Press Play all. The first pair sounds once and lasts two beats, not two separate notes.
The second pair sounds once and lasts four beats.
The curved line is the sign that the second note is not played again.
demonstration.textAlternative: Two pairs of tied notes: crotchet to crotchet (2 beats), and minim to minim (4 beats).

guided.prompt: Write one note that lasts exactly as long as these two tied notes.

music.textAlternative: A minim tied to a minim.

hints: A dot adds half the note's own value.
A tie adds the two values together.
A dot adds half the note's own value.

feedback.correct: The tied notes add up to that one note.

mistakes.halved-or-doubled: That value is twice (or half) as long. Count it in crotchet beats and compare.
mistakes.dot-misread: Remember: a dot adds half of the note's own value. Work out that half, then add it.
mistakes.note-rest-confusion: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.
mistakes.tie-dot-confusion: A tie joins two notes into one sound, so add both values together.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.
